messages:
maria: Heads up — ACME (priority) opened a ticket: after an automatic regional failover to eu-south-1 their integrations started getting JSON parse errors from function-calling responses. They included one example.

support-rep (ACME): "We POST the same call and suddenly the assistant returns malformed function-calls and truncated json. No HTTP errors, request id req-2026-04-02-ACME-zz9. Please advise."

jonah: Router logs show request accepted for redwood-70b-instruct but x-model-served was redwood-7b-legacy-q8. Region hint was eu-south-1 and a capacity shortage triggered fallback.

sam: If the smaller legacy model uses a different tokenization or default function-calling format, the client might receive truncated or mis-encoded JSON. Paste their prompt + observed response.

support-rep: Example payload and response they received:

```
Prompt: "Extract top 3 revenue drivers and return as JSON using function-calls."
Expected (from us-west-2 earlier): {
  "drivers": ["enterprise renewals", "new product launch", "channel expansion"]
}
Observed (eu-south-1 failover): "{\uFFFDdrivers\uFFFD: [\uFFFDenterprise renewals\uFFFD, ...]}"  // non-UTF8, truncated mid-json
Request-id: req-2026-04-02-ACME-zz9
Headers: x-model-requested: redwood-70b-instruct, x-model-served: redwood-7b-legacy-q8, x-route-region: eu-south-1
```

maria: Customer also noted they're billed at our 70B rate for that request but the served model token count and cost should have been 7B — they're asking for a credit and explanation.

ops-oncall: Root cause appears to be routing fallback policy that matches by architecture and 'cost_tier' but not tokenizer_family or function_calling_schema. Fallback selection logic predates tokenizer metadata.

sam: Immediate mitigations:
- For priority orgs, enforce strict tokenizer_family equality when routing fallbacks.
- Add an opt-out header: `X-Fallback-Allow: none|compatible|any` we can honor per-request.
- Add a temporary account-level pin to route ACME back to us-west-2 while we roll fixes.

jonah: Repro steps I used to trigger locally:
1) Set X-Region: eu-south-1 and Accept-Model: redwood-70b-instruct
2) Flood us-west-2 to simulate high load so router routes to failover
3) Observe returned x-model-served header and compare response structure

Curl used:
```
curl -i -H "Authorization: Bearer $REDBOX" \
  -H "X-Region: eu-south-1" \
  -H "Accept-Model: redwood-70b-instruct" \
  -d '{"input":"Extract top 3 revenue drivers and return as JSON using function-calls."}' \
  https://api.redwood.ai/v1/chat
```

ops-oncall: RNWD-2499 opened for routing fallback compatibility. Emergency patch queued to consider `tokenizer_family` and `function_schema_version` during candidate selection. Also adding audit logs when billed model != served model.

deploy-bot: emergency-routing-fix v2.3 deploying to eu-south canary (2/4 nodes) — will monitor 10m.

maria: I've told ACME: (1) We're applying an account-level pin to route them to us-west-2 immediately, (2) rolling emergency routing patch, (3) investigating billing credit for req-2026-04-02-ACME-zz9 and related requests. Provided them the curl repro and asked for any additional failing request ids.

support-rep: Please tag me on RNWD-2499 and confirm when pin is active.

deploy-bot: canary healthy on 2/2, promoting to full. Change id start-1920470012

sam: Postmortem action items: add tokenizer_family to model metadata used by routing, surface mismatch warnings in response headers when served != requested, and add an automated semantic-compatibility smoke test for fallback variants.

maria: Thanks all. Follow-ups: billing ops to confirm credits, product to spec `X-Fallback-Allow`, infra to land RNWD-2499. I'll keep ACME updated.

support-rep: Thank you. :raised_hands:

jonah: I'll paste final logs and billing ops correlation once done.
